title: Household Arts, Vol. III
summary: Every charm a careful housekeeper needs, from the week's first wash to the last of the silver. — M. Voss

pages.text: Twist the cloth three times against the grain {~and name the house aloud~}; the water {~leaves it gladly~}. Hang {~where the wind can find it~}.
{~Lay the cloth flat and work the paste into~} the afflicted area until {~the colour rises into it~}. {~Rinse in cold, and~} do not use near open water.
pages.authorNote: The designer's original example page. Shares eye of newt with Hold Fast on purpose.

pages.text: A kettle so charmed keeps its warmth from {~first light~} to supper. {~Mind the handle~}; {~it remembers the heat longer than the water does~}.
Hang a muslin bag of this in the wardrobe. Moths {~and worse~} keep their distance {~for a season~}.
Whatever this touches {~stays as it is~}: bread will not stale, {~petals will not fall~}, {~ink will not fade~}. {~Never~} upon anything that still breathes {~— it will keep that, too~}.
pages.authorNote: Outlier. Legible text reads '...upon anything that still breathes' without the 'never': ominous, ambiguous.

pages.text: Linen folded under this {~keeps its crease~} for a week {~and its scent for longer~}.
